questions.question: When would you use map, filter, and reduce in JavaScript?
questions.title: map, filter, and reduce
questions.direct_answer: map transforms every item and returns an equally sized array; filter keeps items that pass a predicate; reduce combines items into one result such as a sum, lookup, or grouped object. They do not mutate the source array by themselves.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can choose clear array transformations.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using reduce for every problem or forgetting to return from a map callback.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention immutability, readable callbacks, and using a plain loop when stateful control flow is clearer.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define map, filter, and reduce simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Declarative transformations
sections.content: These methods express intent: map changes shape, filter changes membership, and reduce accumulates a result.

sections.title: A small pipeline
Interview cues
items: map returns one output per input.
reduce needs a clear initial accumulator value.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: I use map for one-to-one transformation, filter to keep matching items, and reduce when I need one accumulated result. The methods return new arrays, so they fit immutable UI state updates when callbacks are pure.

sections.title: Concept explained
sections.content: Walk through the example step by step, then say when this approach is a good fit and what you would test at the boundary.
